verdict.rationale: Obsidian stores vaults as local plain-text Markdown files and works fully offline with no vendor cloud dependency (obsidian-docs-2, obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-23), and it explicitly supports syncing via self-managed backends like Git, Dropbox, iCloud, or OneDrive instead of Obsidian's own service (obsidian-docs-19), corroborated by community use of the Git plugin for backup and users running fully local/self-synced setups (obsidian-comm-8, obsidian-comm-19). However, Obsidian itself ships no first-party self-hosted sync server — Obsidian Sync is a paid cloud add-on (obsidian-docs-9, obsidian-docs-32) — so 'self-hosted backend' relies on bolting on third-party tools rather than an officially supported self-host option. Missing for 10: an official self-hosted Sync server/backend from Obsidian, and independent verification that community sync alternatives (e.g., Git plugin, CRDT collab plugin) fully replace real-time multi-device sync without caveats.
